resources.string: Looks things up, organizes what you care about, and uses apps on your phone.\nSay what you want done and I’ll do it in the background.
A model takes about 2 minutes. Using apps also needs accessibility and a one-time pairing, about 10 minutes the first time. You can skip pairing and still chat, browse, and work with files.
Search and summarize the posts and notes you care about
Taps and types on a background screen. Needs accessibility and a one-time pairing
A built-in browser; spreadsheets and PDFs in a separate environment
Reads your Obsidian notes before each task and writes back after success. You can see what was read and written
X Assistant thinks with your own model service. Connect a provider first, then pick a model for each job.
Only the main model is required; the other two can wait.
Paste the key from your provider
X Assistant lists this provider’s models, then asks one of them to call a test tool; if both work, it’s saved.
The base URL must start with http:// or https://
This address isn’t encrypted; your API key and chats could be seen by others on the network.
Asking %1$s to call a test tool failed: %2$s
%1$s didn’t answer a test tool call within %2$d seconds
%1$s didn’t call the tool. X Assistant needs a model that can call tools to get things done. The provider was saved, but this model wasn’t set as the main model.
127.0.0.1 is this phone. If the server runs on your computer, replace it with the computer’s local network address and let the server accept connections from the network, not only from itself.

No models could be listed at this address. The provider may not offer a model list, or the address or interface type may be wrong. Enter a model name and tap “Test and save” again; one test call will tell.
This provider didn’t list any models. Enter a model name and tap “Test and save” again; it’s saved only if a test call with it works.
Model “%1$s” doesn’t exist. Enter the full model ID from the provider’s docs (%2$s).
No models could be listed, and a test call with “%1$s” wasn’t found either: the address or interface type is probably wrong, or there is no such model (model names look like: %2$s).
%1$s didn’t call the tool. X Assistant needs a model that can call tools to get things done; pick another main model.
This is %1$s’s official address. Its preset fills in the address and interface type for you.
The interface type doesn’t match either: %1$s uses the %2$s interface, but %3$s is selected.
This account hasn’t activated “%1$s” or has no access to it (the provider says: %2$s). Pick another model, or activate it in the provider’s console.
this account hasn’t activated this model or has no access to it (the provider says: %1$s)
the provider has no such model
it doesn’t call tools, and X Assistant needs a model that can call tools
The provider is connected, but “%1$s” didn’t pass the test: %2$s. Pick a model from the list that your account has activated.
Tried %1$s; none of them is activated.
Tried %1$s; none of them passed the test.
%1$s, tried first, didn’t pass the test: %2$s. The main model is “%3$s”, which passed.
You can sign up on your phone. On save, X Assistant tries deepseek-chat and one tool call, and uses it as the main model only if that passes. This provider is already selected below.
If it fails: check the key was copied in full, confirm deepseek-chat is enabled in the DeepSeek console, or pick another provider above and test again.
This one only needs the model. It does not use apps or a knowledge base. Tap once to see how X Assistant answers.
In three sentences, tell me what you can help with. If phone control is not paired yet, and if no knowledge base is selected, say what happens in one sentence each.
To use apps or notes, finish this once, then add them in Settings.
